title: Aerial trapping and analysis of moth pheromone compounds via GC-MS
author: Ghosh, Palazzo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare standard solutions
steps.instruction: Weigh ~1 mg of each analytical standard and dissolve in enough n‑hexane to obtain a concentration of 10 µg/µL; dilute each 10 µg/µL solution 100‑fold with n‑hexane to 0.1 µg/µL, vortexing vigorously after each dilution; then mix 10 µL of each 0.1 µg/µL solution and bring the volume to 1000 µL with n‑hexane (for four standards add 960 µL n‑hexane to 40 µL mix) to give a 1 mg/L working solution (adjust concentration as needed for the experiment).

substeps.instruction: Weigh ~1 mg of each analytical standard.
Dissolve in n‑hexane to reach 10 µg/µL.
Make a 100× dilution with n‑hexane to obtain 0.1 µg/µL; vortex vigorously after each dilution.
Combine 10 µL of each 0.1 µg/µL solution and add n‑hexane to a final volume of 1000 µL (e.g., 960 µL n‑hexane + 40 µL mix for four standards) to produce a 1 mg/L working solution.

steps.title: Spike Tenax cartridges with standards
steps.instruction: Using the 1 mg/L working solution, pipette volumes that correspond to 1, 10, 20, 50 and 200 ng onto separate Tenax TA cartridges, attach each cartridge’s unridged end to a suction pump with PVC tubing, set the pump flow to 400 mL/min, and aspirate for 1 min; perform each amount in triplicate (three cartridges per amount).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the volume of 1 mg/L solution needed for 1 ng, 10 ng, 20 ng, 50 ng and 200 ng.
Using a micropipette, add the calculated volume into the crimped end of each Tenax TA cartridge.
Connect the unridged end of each cartridge to a suction pump via PVC tube.
Start the pump at 400 mL/min and let it aspirate for 1 min.
Repeat steps a–d three times for each target amount to obtain triplicates.

steps.title: Inject spiked cartridges into GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Insert each cartridge that has been spiked with the standard solution into the GC‑MS system and run the injection using the same method described for cartridge analysis in the protocol.

steps.title: Generate standard curve from GC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Integrate the peak areas of the calibration standards and of the compounds of interest in Agilent MassHunter; record triplicate area values for each standard, plot area versus amount, ensure the coefficient of determination (R²) exceeds 0.9, and obtain the linear equation y = a x + b.

substeps.instruction: Open the GC‑MS data in Agilent MassHunter.
Integrate peak areas for each calibration standard and for each target compound.
Collect the area values for each standard in triplicate.
Plot area (y) versus amount (x) and fit a linear regression; verify R² > 0.9.
Record the slope (a) and intercept (b) of the line (y = a x + b).

steps.title: Calculate compound amounts
steps.instruction: For each compound of interest, compute its amount using x = (y − b)/a, where y is the measured peak area and a and b are from the standard‑curve equation.

steps.title: Determine retention indices
steps.instruction: Spike a Tenax TA cartridge with 10 µL of a commercial n‑alkane mixture, inject it into the GC‑MS using the same method as above, record the retention times of each n‑alkane, then calculate the Kovats retention index for each target compound with I_T = 100 z + 100 (T_i − T_z)/(T_{z+1} − T_z), where z and z+1 are the carbon numbers of the bracketing alkanes.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of a commercial n‑alkane solution to a Tenax TA cartridge.
Inject the cartridge into the GC‑MS using the same procedure as for standards.
Obtain retention times (T) for all n‑alkanes.
Identify the two n‑alkanes that bracket each compound of interest (with carbon numbers z and z+1).
Calculate the Kovats index using the formula I_T = 100 z + 100 (T_i − T_z)/(T_{z+1} − T_z).
